items.title: Section: Chapter Four Opens — Twelve Bodhisattva Abodes Comprehensively Gathering Everything Already Explained, Plus the Thirteenth Abode of the Tathagata

items.zh: 如是始從種性具足，廣說乃至於如所說菩薩所學，正勤修學；於如所說菩薩諸相，正等顯現；於諸菩薩分加行中，正勤修學；於如所說菩薩意樂，能淨修治。諸菩薩眾略有菩薩十二種住。由此菩薩十二種住，普攝一切諸菩薩住，普攝一切諸菩薩行。復有如來第十三住。由此住故，現前等覺廣大菩提，名無上住。
items.en:
Within the Basic Section, the Bodhisattva Stage, the second yoga foundation of sustained practice, chapter four, the first part: the abodes.
This means that, beginning from being complete with the lineage, extensively explained through diligently training in what a bodhisattva should learn as already explained, correctly and equally manifesting the marks of a bodhisattva as already explained, diligently training in the applied efforts within the divisions of a bodhisattva as already explained, and being able to genuinely purify and cultivate the excellent aspiration of a bodhisattva as already explained — bodhisattvas, in brief, have twelve kinds of abode. Through these twelve kinds of abode, every bodhisattva abode is comprehensively gathered in, and every bodhisattva practice is comprehensively gathered in.
Commentary: Regarding "comprehensively gathered in, every bodhisattva abode" and the like — a bodhisattva's cultivation of every undertaking has two distinct occasions: first, the time of moving; second, the time of abiding still. As it is said, a bodhisattva cultivates freedom from heedlessness in accordance with however one should move, and in accordance with however one should abide still, moving in just this way and abiding still in just this way, without any violation. Such moving and abiding still, in brief, comprehensively gather in every undertaking of a bodhisattva. It is on this basis that the twelve kinds of bodhisattva abode are established, and it is said that they comprehensively gather in every instance of such moving and abiding still.
There is, furthermore, a thirteenth abode belonging to the tathagata. Through this abode, one manifests directly before the mind the vast, equal awakening to great awakening itself — this is called the unsurpassed abode.

items.title: Section: All Thirteen Abodes Named in a Single Summary Verse, From the Lineage Through Final Buddhahood

items.zh: 云何菩薩十二住等？嗢拕南曰：種性、勝解行、極喜、增上戒、增上心、三慧、無相有功用、無相無功用、及以無礙解、最上菩薩住，最極如來住。
items.en: What are these twelve bodhisattva abodes, and so forth? A summary verse states: "The lineage, resolute practice; utmost joy, excellent discipline; excellent mind, three [abodes of] wisdom; mark-free with effortful application; mark-free without effortful application; and also unobstructed understanding; the most excellent bodhisattva abode; the most ultimate tathagata abode."

items.title: Section: All Twelve Bodhisattva Abodes Named in Full, Each Briefly Defined and Mapped to Its Corresponding Ground

items.zh: 謂菩薩種性住、勝解行住、極歡喜住、增上戒住、增上心住。增上慧住。復有三種：一、覺分相應增上慧住，二、諸諦相應增上慧住，三、緣起流轉止息相應增上慧住。謂諸菩薩如實了知能觀真實、所觀真實，及於真實諸有情類，由無智故眾苦流轉，由有智故眾苦止息。如是菩薩，由於三門以慧觀察，故有三種增上慧住。及有加行有功用無間缺道運轉無相住、無加行無功用無間缺道運轉無相住、無礙解住、最上成滿菩薩住。是名菩薩十二種住。如是菩薩十二種住，普攝一切諸菩薩住，普攝一切諸菩薩行。
items.en:
This means: the abode of the lineage; the abode of resolute practice; the abode of utmost joy; the abode of excellent moral discipline; the abode of excellent mind. The abode of excellent wisdom further comprises three: first, the abode of excellent wisdom associated with the factors of awakening; second, the abode of excellent wisdom associated with the truths; third, the abode of excellent wisdom associated with the stilling of the flow of dependent origination. This means that bodhisattvas genuinely, correctly know the wisdom that observes reality and the reality observed, and know that, among the classes of sentient beings involved with that same reality, it is through lack of wisdom that manifold suffering continues to circulate, and through possessing wisdom that manifold suffering comes to rest. Because bodhisattvas observe through these three approaches by means of wisdom, there are three abodes of excellent wisdom. There is furthermore the mark-free abode with effortful, uninterrupted application in motion; the abode without marks and without effortful, uninterrupted application in motion; the abode of unobstructed understanding; and the most excellent, fully accomplished bodhisattva abode. These are called the bodhisattva's twelve kinds of abode.
These twelve kinds of bodhisattva abode, in this way, comprehensively gather in every bodhisattva abode, and comprehensively gather in every bodhisattva practice.

items.title: Section: The Tathagata's Own Abode Deferred to a Later Chapter — the Abode of the Lineage Opens With Its First Mark, an Inborn Kindness Never Taught

items.zh: 如來住者，謂過一切諸菩薩住，現前等覺大菩提住。此中最後如來住者，於後究竟瑜伽處最後建立品，當具演說。菩薩所有十二種住，如所安立，我今當說。云何菩薩種性住？云何菩薩住種性住？謂諸菩薩住種性住，性自仁賢，性自成就菩薩功德；菩薩所應眾多善法，於彼現行亦有顯現。由性仁賢逼遣方便，令於善轉，非由思擇有所制約、有所防護。
items.en:
The tathagata's own abode surpasses every bodhisattva abode, manifesting directly before the mind the great awakening itself. This final, tathagata abode will be fully explained within the later chapter on establishment, in the yoga foundation of ultimate practice.
I shall now explain the bodhisattva's twelve kinds of abode, exactly as they have been established.
What is the bodhisattva's abode of the lineage? How does a bodhisattva abide within the abode of the lineage?
This means that bodhisattvas abiding in the abode of the lineage are, by inborn nature, kind and virtuous, spontaneously accomplished in the qualities proper to a bodhisattva; the many wholesome teachings proper to a bodhisattva are also displayed in that bodhisattva's own visible conduct. Through this inborn kindness and virtue, such a bodhisattva is compelled towards wholesome action by its own natural means, not through deliberate reflection producing any restraint or guarding.
Commentary: Regarding "by inborn nature, kind and virtuous" and the like — this means that bodhisattvas, through their own already-accomplished inborn nature, hold a mind that is warm and gentle, a mind that is genuinely pure; anger and the wish to harm do not persist for long, arising and then being relinquished as soon as they arise, giving rise instead to a kind, virtuous mind — this is called being, by inborn nature, kind and virtuous. Relying on this lineage, such a bodhisattva has genuine capacity and great strength, able to sever both the afflictive and cognitive obscurations and realise unsurpassed, correct, complete awakening — this is why it is said that such a bodhisattva's inborn nature spontaneously accomplishes the qualities proper to a bodhisattva. Possessing the characteristic seed-potential of the six perfections, by virtue of which others recognise this person as a genuine bodhisattva, is what is meant by the many wholesome teachings proper to a bodhisattva being displayed in that bodhisattva's own visible conduct.

items.title: Section: Already Possessing Every Buddha-Seed, and a Nature Naturally Free of Coarse Affliction — Closing the Abode of the Lineage in Full

items.zh: 若諸菩薩住種性住，任持一切佛法種子，於自體中、於所依中，已具足有一切佛法一切種子。又諸菩薩住種性住，性離麁垢，不能現起上煩惱纏。由此纏故，造無間業，或斷善根。如種性品所說種種住種性相，於此菩薩種性住中，亦應廣說，應如實知。是名菩薩種性住。
items.en:
If bodhisattvas abide in the abode of the lineage, they sustain every seed of every buddha-quality; within their own body and mind, and within the basis that supports them, every seed of every buddha-quality is already fully present.
Furthermore, bodhisattvas abiding in the abode of the lineage are, by nature, free of coarse defilement, incapable of giving rise to severe afflictive entanglement — the kind of entanglement that would produce an act of immediate retribution, or sever wholesome roots altogether.
The various marks of abiding in the lineage already explained in the chapter on the lineage should likewise be explained at length within this account of the bodhisattva's abode of the lineage; one should genuinely understand them accordingly.
This, then, is called a bodhisattva's abode of the lineage.

items.title: Section: The Abode of Resolute Practice — Every Bodhisattva Practice From First Arousing the Aspiration Until Pure Aspiration Is Attained

items.zh: 云何菩薩勝解行住？謂諸菩薩，從初發心乃至未得清淨意樂，所有一切諸菩薩行，當知皆名勝解行住。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's abode of resolute practice? This means that every bodhisattva practice whatsoever, from the very first arousing of the aspiration for awakening up until pure aspiration has not yet been attained, one should understand, is called the abode of resolute practice.

items.title: Section: A Second, Dynamic Pass — How a Bodhisattva Actually Moves From the Lineage Through the First Four Abodes, Each Stage Already Setting Forth Towards the Next

items.zh: 又諸菩薩種性住中，於餘十一諸菩薩住及如來住唯有因轉，攝受彼因。於餘所有諸菩薩住尚未發趣、未得、未淨，況如來住。若諸菩薩勝解行住，普於一切餘菩薩住及如來住，皆名發趣，未得、未淨。即於如是勝解行住，亦名發趣、亦名為得，為令清淨而修正行。
items.en:
Furthermore, while bodhisattvas are in the abode of the lineage, with respect to the remaining eleven bodhisattva abodes and the tathagata's own abode, only the cause is operating — the cause for them is being gathered in. With respect to all the remaining bodhisattva abodes, such a bodhisattva has not yet set forth towards them, not yet attained them, and not yet purified them — how much less the tathagata's own abode.
If bodhisattvas are in the abode of resolute practice, with respect to all the remaining bodhisattva abodes and the tathagata's own abode, they are universally said to have set forth towards them, though not yet attained or purified them. With respect to this very abode of resolute practice itself, they are said both to have set forth towards it and to have attained it, cultivating correct practice specifically in order to bring it to purity.

items.title: Section: The Same Pattern Extends Through Utmost Joy, Excellent Discipline, and by Analogy All the Way to the Tenth Ground

items.zh: 勝解行住既清淨已，極歡喜住先已發趣，今復名得，為令清淨而修正行。極歡喜住既清淨已，增上戒住先已發趣，今復名得，為令清淨而修正行。如是廣說，展轉乃至最上成滿菩薩住。
items.en:
Once the abode of resolute practice has been purified, the abode of utmost joy, already set forth towards, is now also called attained, and correct practice is cultivated in order to bring it to purity.
Once the abode of utmost joy has been purified, the abode of excellent moral discipline, already set forth towards, is now also called attained, and correct practice is cultivated in order to bring it to purity.
Extensively explained in this way, the same pattern continues in turn all the way to the most excellent, fully accomplished bodhisattva abode.

items.title: Section: Sudden, Instantaneous Attainment at Buddhahood, Contrasted With the Bodhisattva's Own Gradual Attainment Across Three Great Incalculable Eons

items.zh: 即此最上成滿菩薩住既清淨已，從此無間，其如來住先已發趣，當知於今頓得、頓淨。是如來住於菩薩住，當知此中如是差別。
items.en:
Once this very most excellent, fully accomplished bodhisattva abode has been purified, the tathagata's own abode, already set forth towards from the beginning, is, from this point without any interval, now attained — one should understand that both this attainment and this purification occur suddenly.
This is the difference to be understood between the tathagata's own abode and the bodhisattva abodes.
Commentary: Regarding "sudden attainment, sudden purification" — within the most excellent, fully accomplished bodhisattva abode, the fruit of cultivation reaches its own completion, and the tathagata's own abode is obtained without any interval, both the afflictive and cognitive obscurations purified without interval as well; from that time onward, no further cultivation whatsoever remains to be done — this is why it is called sudden attainment, sudden purification. This differs from the gradual attainment, gradual purification found within each individual bodhisattva abode already described; one should understand this distinction accordingly.

items.title: Section: A Third, Intrinsic Pass Begins — Utmost Joy's Own Clarified Aspiration, and Excellent Discipline's Own Innate Precept-Nature

items.zh: 云何菩薩極歡喜住？謂諸菩薩淨勝意樂住。云何菩薩增上戒住？謂諸菩薩，淨勝意樂為緣，所得性戒相應住。
items.en:
What is a bodhisattva's abode of utmost joy? It is a bodhisattva's abode of pure, excellent aspiration.
What is a bodhisattva's abode of excellent moral discipline? It is the abode where, taking pure, excellent aspiration as its condition, a bodhisattva abides joined with the innate precept-nature thereby attained.
Commentary: Regarding "taking pure, excellent aspiration as its condition" and the like — as the text itself explains further below: at the abode of utmost joy, through ten kinds of mental aspiration, purity of aspiration has already been attained. And so on, extensively explained — it is precisely because these same ten kinds of aspiration have reached their superior grade, brought to the very fullest completion, that bodhisattvas enter and realise the second abode, excellent moral discipline. Within this abode, the innate precept-nature is complete; not even the very slightest unwholesome course of action belonging to precept-violation manifests, let alone one of middling or superior grade. Furthermore, with respect to the ten complete courses of wholesome action, their own intrinsic nature manifests spontaneously. This should be understood according to that fuller explanation.

blocks.text: Chapter four, on the "abodes" (住), retells the whole bodhisattva path as twelve stages plus a thirteenth, the Tathāgata's own. These correspond closely to the ten grounds you may know from the *Daśabhūmika Sūtra*.

"There is also the Tathāgata's thirteenth abode, through which vast awakening is directly realised." Venerable Miào Jìng: 行 (conduct) is the time of practising, the cause; 住 (abiding) is the result. Practising daily sitting and then attaining access concentration is "abiding".

Venerable Miào Jìng: at the seventh ground, calm and insight on ultimate truth is uninterrupted. Master Cháng Bǎi: special effort is still required for this mark-free abiding. (Ru-Yi's "with marks" mistranslates 無相, "mark-free".)

"This final Tathāgata abode will be fully explained in the last chapter." The lineage bodhisattva has an inborn kindness never taught: Venerable Miào Jìng, 仁 is love and 賢 is goodness; their conscience compels them. Master Cháng Bǎi: though not yet in contact with Buddhism, their nature is already gentle and good.
"Unable to give rise to severe entanglements that would produce acts of immediate retribution or sever wholesome roots." Venerable Miào Jìng: they have afflictions, but not the most serious bondage.
Master Cháng Bǎi: this abode includes the provisions and preparation stages, requiring one incalculable eon.

Venerable Miào Jìng: "sudden purification" is cutting delusion, "sudden attainment" is realising truth. Master Cháng Bǎi: at the final vajra mind, purity is attained all at once, yet only after three incalculable eons.
Venerable Miào Jìng: the mind naturally manifests this way; that is why the innate precepts are complete.
Notice the bodhisattva of lineage: good-natured before ever meeting Buddhism. Both teachers see this kind of person everywhere. You may know some.

quiz.q: The abodes chapter speaks of "行時" and "住時," rendered "moving" and "abiding still." How do the lectures explain them?
options: Miào Jìng: "行" is practising (cause), "住" is abiding in the result — like attaining access concentration after daily sitting; Cháng Bǎi: all bodhisattva work has these two times
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "行" is the time of practising — the cause; "住" is the result, abiding in it — practising daily sitting and then attaining access concentration is "abiding." Master Cháng Bǎi: all bodhisattva work has these two times. The English "moving / still" misses this.

quiz.q: Beyond the twelve bodhisattva abodes there is the Tathāgata's thirteenth. What is it called?
options: the unsurpassed abode — directly awakening to vast awakening
quiz.why: "There is also the Tathāgata's thirteenth abode, through which vast awakening is directly realised — called the unsurpassed abode." Venerable Miào Jìng: twelve bodhisattva abodes plus the Tathāgata's make thirteen.

quiz.q: "The mark-free abode with effort and application" is rendered "abode with marks…." What do the lectures say?
options: it is mark-free, only still requiring effort — Miào Jìng: the seventh ground's calm and insight on ultimate truth is uninterrupted; Cháng Bǎi: special effort is still needed to reach uninterrupted mark-free abiding
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: at the seventh ground, calm and insight on ultimate truth is uninterrupted. Master Cháng Bǎi: special effort is still required to reach uninterrupted mark-free abiding. The English "with marks" is a mistranslation of 無相.

quiz.q: Where does the treatise say the Tathāgata's abode will be fully explained?
options: in the final chapter on establishment in the yoga foundation of ultimate practice
quiz.why: "This final Tathāgata abode will be fully explained in the last chapter, on establishment, in the yoga foundation of ultimate practice." Master Cháng Bǎi: the Tathāgata's abode surpasses every bodhisattva abode.

quiz.q: Lineage-abiding bodhisattvas are "by nature kind and virtuous." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain this, and what drives their goodness?
options: 仁 is love, 賢 is goodness — their kind nature, their conscience, compels them
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: 仁 is love — compassion; 賢 is goodness; their kind nature, their conscience, compels them. Master Cháng Bǎi: though not yet in contact with Buddhism, their nature is already gentle and good.

quiz.q: Lineage-abiding bodhisattvas are "free of coarse defilement" — incapable of what?
options: severe entanglement that would cause an act of immediate retribution or sever wholesome roots
quiz.why: "Free of coarse defilement, unable to give rise to severe entanglements that would produce acts of immediate retribution or sever wholesome roots." Venerable Miào Jìng: they have afflictions, but not the most serious bondage.

quiz.q: How do the lectures define the scope of the abode of resolute practice?
options: both: the provisions and preparation stages, from first resolve until pure aspiration; Cháng Bǎi adds one incalculable eon
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: it includes bodhisattvas at the provisions and preparation stages, requiring one incalculable eon. Venerable Miào Jìng: the provisions stage and the preparation stage together are the abode of resolute practice.

quiz.q: After the highest bodhisattva abode, the Tathāgata's abode is "suddenly attained, suddenly purified." How do the lectures explain?
options: Miào Jìng: sudden purity is cutting delusion, sudden attainment is realising truth; Cháng Bǎi: at the final vajra-like mind all is complete at once — bodhisattva abodes are gradual
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "sudden purification" is cutting delusion, "sudden attainment" is realising truth. Master Cháng Bǎi: at the final vajra mind, purity is attained suddenly, all complete at once — yet only after three incalculable eons.
